title: Selective publication of antidepressant trials and its influence on apparent efficacy: Updated comparisons and meta-analyses of newer versus older trials
authors: Turner EH, Cipriani A, Furukawa TA, Salanti G, de Vries YA
population: FDA-registered phase II and III placebo-controlled trials of 4 antidepressants approved 2008 to 2013, compared with 74 trials of 12 older antidepressants
funder: The authors received no specific funding for this work.
authorConflicts: Turner previously worked as an FDA medical officer. Outside the submitted work, Cipriani received research and consultancy fees from INCiPiT, CARIPLO Foundation and Angelini Pharma; Furukawa received grants and personal fees from Mitsubishi-Tanabe and Shionogi and personal fees from MSD; Salanti received fees paid to the University of Bern from Biogen and Merck.
result: 30 trials of newer antidepressants with 13,747 patients. Transparent publication of FDA-negative trials rose from 11% for older antidepressants to 47% (7 of 15) for newer ones; all 15 FDA-positive newer trials were published transparently. Effect size inflation (journal minus FDA Hedges g) was 0.05 (0.29 versus 0.24) for newer and 0.10 (0.41 versus 0.31) for older antidepressants.
